§ion;
At a Mexican restaurant that we love, we built up a relationship with one of the waitresses. At one point she came over to our house and made us a Mexican meal from scratch.
It was so AWESOME, that Ransom and Di had her come back over and make it again so he could write down what she did and create this recipe.
NOTE:
"Of Comfort" translated to Spanish is "de Consuelo".
But when translating it back to English "De Consuelo" may mean "From Consuelo".
And since this recipe is from Consuelo… &smiley;
Olive Oil3 Tablespoons
WaterHOT 4 Cups
Chicken Bouillon1½ Tablespoons Roma Tomato1 Onion½ Tomato Paste2 teaspoons Rice2 Cups
GarlicMinced 1 Tablespoon
In a bowl, mix Water and Chicken Bouillon then set it aside. Slice Roma Tomato into ¼-inch disks, then slice the disks into quarters. Slice Onion into ¼-inch disks, then cut the disks into ⅛ths.
Put Oil in a skillet and tip it around until bottom is covered. Put Skillet on a burner at medium-high. Add Onion and saut&eAcute; for 2 minutes. Add Garlic (minced) and saut&eAcute; for another minute. Add Rice and saut&eAcute; for another minute.
Add all other ingredients and stir well, then cover with skillet's lid. DO NOT REMOVE LID OR STIR UNTIL DONE!!!
Turn burner to medium and simmer for 15-20 minutes. DO NOT REMOVE LID OR STIR UNTIL DONE!!!
Remove skillet from burner then stir gently, scraping the bottom.
While cooking, DO NOT REMOVE LID OR STIR UNTIL DONE!!!
If doubling the recipe, it will generally take about 10 minutes longer to simmmer.
Final Note: While cooking, DO NOT REMOVE LID OR STIR UNTIL DONE!!!
